parts.title: PART 2
parts.instructions: For each question, choose the correct answer. (5 Questions)
parts.passage_subtitle: 14-year-old Marc Weiner has his own cooking show on TV.
parts.passage_text:
Marc, when did you start cooking?
I started helping my mum in the kitchen when I was six. I made her coffee – it was terrible! I was seven when I made my first meal – a pizza with four different kinds of cheese.

Do you have a favourite recipe?
It's hard because I have so many. The easy ones are fun – things with pasta, tomatoes and onions. My favourites are the ones that include fish. There are so many different things you can do!

What do your parents think of your cooking?
When I won my first competition, my mum and dad understood that I was a real chef. They're glad that they don't have to make dinner every night, and they enjoy my food – usually! But, you can't make everyone happy all the time.

What's the best way to get good at cooking?
First, I threw away some of what I made because it was no good – that's how you learn. Then, I did it differently the next time. You need to practise, so if you know a chef, ask if you can help them in the kitchen sometimes.

Finally, what's it like being on TV?
It's interesting. I'm actually a very quiet person, so I'm amazed that I really enjoy myself making the shows. They're watched by millions, but I still find it strange when people I don't know say hello to me in the street.

parts.title: Part 1
parts.instructions: For each question, choose the correct picture.

questions.question: When is Holly visiting her friend in Japan?
questions.transcript:
Boy: When are you going to Japan? Is it in March?
Holly: No, I'm going after that. In August.
Boy: Oh, lovely. What clothes are you taking?
Holly: Well, it won't be cold and I'll be back before the autumn.
Boy: Summer will be lovely in Japan.
Holly: I know, I can't wait!

Diego: It's half past three.

parts.title: Part 2
parts.instructions: For each question, choose the correct answer.
parts.context: You will hear Luis talking to his sister about some places they could go to. What problem is there in each place?
parts.source_url_note: Matches EnglishPracticeTest KET Listening Test (Part 5 in standard KET)
parts.transcript:
Girl: Hey Luis! How about doing something this afternoon? Would you like to play tennis at the local court?
Luis: I'd love to, but it's going to rain.
Girl: Well, let's do something indoors. The pool is open at weekends.
Luis: No way! Last time I went there the water was green! I'm sure they haven't cleaned it yet!
Girl: There's always the cafe in Elm Square. Let's go for a coffee.
Luis: That's not a good idea on a Saturday! It's full of people! It will take ages to get a seat!
Girl: Hey! I heard there's a good film at the cinema.
Luis: Sorry, I can't do that this week. It's £8 a ticket and I've got no money left.
Girl: OK. Well, that leaves the park, but I'm not sure it's warm enough to spend so much time outside.
Luis: You're right, it's freezing! I suppose we'll just have to stay at home, even though there's nothing to do here!

parts.context: You will hear Vivien and Tom talking about their meals last night.

questions.question: The table in Vivien's restaurant was

options.A: had special food for people like Monica.
options.B: had a lot of dishes on the menu.

options.A: the dessert was the best part of the meal.
options.B: everything was delicious, but not the dessert.
options.C: the food was delicious, but the dessert wasn't as good as the rest of the meal.

options.A: paid too much for his meal.
options.B: paid less than the full price for his meal.
options.C: fixed the problem with the bill after half an hour.

parts.transcript:
Vivien: Hi Tom.
Tom: Hi Vivien. How was your meal last night?
Vivien: Actually, it didn't go too well. Firstly, we couldn't get around the table. We'd booked for six people, but eight came.
Tom: Oh dear!
Vivien: Then they didn't have anything for Monica to eat.
Tom: She doesn't eat meat or fish, does she?
Vivien: That's right. She's a vegetarian. She wasn't happy! Then they brought Mark the wrong dish. He ordered steak but they brought him chicken, so he sent it back, and then he had to wait again for his steak. What about your meal?
Tom: The food was delicious, especially the dessert. Everything was perfect — until the bill arrived.
Vivien: Was it expensive?
Tom: Well, it was quite expensive, but we knew that from before. The problem was they gave us the bill for a different table. It took half an hour for them to fix the problem! In the end, they gave us a discount because of all the problems with the bill.

parts.title: Part 4
parts.instructions: For each question, write the correct answer in the gap. Write ONE WORD or a number or a date or a time. (5 questions)
parts.context: You will hear a teacher talking to a group of students about a summer course.

questions.label: Students must not be older than
Students have to be good at

parts.transcript:
Most students in this college study in Brighton Summer School during the summer holidays and really enjoy it. So I'm going to tell you a bit about their summer school.
Courses start on the twentieth of June so you can choose any date that suits you until August the 15th. Most students choose courses in the middle of July as the weather's better then.
Courses are available for students who are between eighteen and twenty five years old.
But to work there as an assistant during your studies, you have to be at least twenty-two. You don't need to be good at sports or other languages, but they need you to speak good English. That's because all classes will be in English. Each day you'll get some homework and during your time there you'll need to do two group projects, one each week.
If you're interested, you need to email me at jessyjones@mail.com — that's J-E-DOUBLE-S-Y-J-O-N-E-S — telling me why you'd like to go.
